A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of masked diffusion models and retain the central TER/SER theory. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 report original formal-language training experiments, MDLM-OWT text-generation evaluations, and GSM8K evaluations, including quality and efficiency results.

after.justification: Sections 3 and 5 and Appendix A report original formal-language experiments and Dream/LLaDA evaluations on GSM8K and MBPP, including accuracy and execution-time measurements.

M1.justification: The analyzed MDM framework, factorized denoising, ELBO training, and synthetic-language generation algorithms remain unchanged. Larger Transformer configurations are experimental settings. The additional decoding strategies are existing methods evaluated or analyzed, rather than newly proposed method components.

E1.justification: V2 removes the free-text generation experiment using OpenWebText-trained MDLM-OWT and adds MBPP program synthesis. GSM8K mathematical reasoning and 2-, 3-, 4-gram and HMM generation remain. This substantially changes the natural-language task coverage.

E2.justification: The GPT2-medium text-generation baseline disappears, and the GSM8K comparator changes from Qwen2-Math-1.5B to Qwen2.5-7B. V2 additionally evaluates left-to-right decoding of Dream-v0-Base-7B and LLaDA-8B-Base as within-model baselines on GSM8K and MBPP. Matched autoregressive baselines remain in the synthetic experiments.

E3.justification: Formal-language settings change from length 512, hidden size 512, eight heads and eight layers (ten for 4-grams) to lengths 512/1024/2048, hidden size 768, twelve heads and ten layers. Timing batch size changes from 16 to 1, and reported sampling steps from 8–2048 to 128–2048. New large-model protocols specify eight-shot GSM8K, three-shot MBPP, and relative accuracy and measured runtime.

E4.justification: V1 primarily sweeps sampling steps at one formal-language sequence length. V2 Table 1 adds joint length/step sensitivity analysis, directly examining TER stability and SER deterioration with length. Figures 1–2 also compare recommended sampling against each checkpoint's left-to-right decoder, testing decoder effects while controlling for model and training differences.

E5.justification: V1 reports averages over 2000 generated sequences without repeated-run uncertainty or significance testing. V2 Appendix F.2 first discloses five runs and mean/standard-deviation reporting; Table 1 adds these uncertainties and t-test-based highlighting against AR baselines. This establishes new reporting, not an increase over a documented v1 run count.

E6.justification: Results are substantially replaced and expanded. V1 Section 5.2 reports AR-like perplexity at roughly 64 steps; v2 reports roughly 512 under its revised model and length settings, so this is not a matched-setting deterioration. V2 Table 2 adds timings, including 4.7 seconds for MDM versus 7.0 for AR at length 2048. New GSM8K/MBPP plots show Dream/LLaDA below Qwen2.5-7B in both accuracy and efficiency, and no joint improvement over their own sequential decoders; v1's natural-language curves are removed.

T1.justification: The original assumptions, TER/SER definitions, Theorems 4.2–4.4, and their proofs are retained. V2 Appendix E.3 substantially broadens the analysis to remasking: it introduces the ReMDM transition law, proves a last-sampling probability lemma (E.10), and argues that the SER lower bound extends to this setting. V1 has no corresponding remasking analysis.

C1.justification: The central metric-dependent efficiency claim remains. V2's abstract and introduction explicitly qualify the linear sampling-step requirement as a worst-case result, narrowing v1's broader wording. They also foreground the empirical claim that current large MDMs have unfavorable reasoning accuracy/cost trade-offs.

C2.justification: V1 cautions that its GSM8K baseline uses different experimental settings. V2 identifies differing private pretraining datasets as a specific confound and motivates within-checkpoint controls. Appendix A.1 additionally explains that LLaDA's sequential configuration does not stop at EOS and can increase runtime. The limitations concerning HMMs and other diffusion families remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix A and Tables 3–4 document model-specific sampling implementations, block lengths, temperatures, top-p, prompting and generation limits, evaluation libraries, and timing on eight RTX 4090 GPUs. Appendix F records revised synthetic-model and timing configurations. The added checklist explicitly defers code/data release until publication; v1 provides no corresponding release statement.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds recent large diffusion models and remasking/token-ordering work, and explicitly distinguishes this paper's inference trade-off analysis from Li et al. (2024)'s learning/statistical-complexity focus. References associated with the removed GPT2/OpenWebText/SlimPajama experiments disappear. The overall research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and experimental narrative are substantially rewritten. Large-model observations now motivate the theory in Section 3 instead of following it in v1 Section 6. Metric and caching discussions are consolidated in Appendix B, experimental appendices are reorganized, and a conference checklist is added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Formal-language bar charts are replaced by length-by-step result tables with uncertainty and significance highlighting, plus a timing table. Large-model curves are replaced by relative accuracy/efficiency scatterplots, and protocol tables are added. The dependency illustration is retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important weaknesses in v1's validation: Table 1 directly tests sequence-length scaling instead of using one length, adds repeated-run uncertainty, and Figures 1–2 introduce within-checkpoint decoding controls that reduce cross-model confounding. The worst-case qualification improves claim precision, and Appendix E.3 extends the theoretical scope. Removing the OpenWebText fluency experiment weakens natural-text support for the positive claim, but the stronger testing of the central efficiency trade-off provides a substantial net improvement.
